audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Jerusalem entry, colt, Hosanna, fig tree frame, temple action, house of prayer/cave of robbers, trust/prayer, forgiveness, and authority dispute.

verses.restored: When they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the Mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples

familiar.text: And when they came nigh to Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, he sendeth forth two of his disciples,

modern.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples

original.text: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ

verses.restored: and says to them, Go into the village opposite you, and immediately entering it you will find a colt tied, on which no human has yet sat. Loose it and bring it.

familiar.text: And saith unto them, Go your way into the village over against you: and as soon as ye be entered into it, ye shall find a colt tied, whereon never man sat; loose him, and bring him.

modern.text: and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς αὐτὴν εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφʼ ὃν οὐδεὶς ⸀οὔπω ἀνθρώπων ⸀ἐκάθισεν· ⸂λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ φέρετε⸃.

verses.restored: If anyone says to you, Why are you doing this? say, The Lord has need of it, and immediately he sends it back here.

familiar.text: And if any man say unto you, Why do ye this? say ye that the Lord hath need of him; and straightway he will send him hither.

modern.text: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.’”

original.text: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τί ποιεῖτε τοῦτο; εἴπατε ⸀ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει· καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἀποστέλλει ⸀πάλιν ὧδε.

verses.restored: They went and found a colt tied at a door outside in the street, and they loose it.

familiar.text: And they went their way, and found the colt tied by the door without in a place where two ways met; and they loose him.

modern.text: So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it,

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἀπῆλθον⸃ καὶ εὗρον πῶλον δεδεμένον ⸀πρὸς θύραν ἔξω ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀμφόδου, καὶ λύουσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Some standing there said to them, What are you doing, loosing the colt?

familiar.text: And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt?

modern.text: and some who were standing there asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”

original.text: καί τινες τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἔλεγον αὐτοῖς· Τί ποιεῖτε λύοντες τὸν πῶλον;

verses.restored: They said to them just as Jesus had said, and they allowed them to go.

familiar.text: And they said unto them even as Jesus had commanded: and they let them go.

modern.text: The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς καθὼς ⸀εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἀφῆκαν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: They bring the colt to Jesus, throw their garments on it, and he sat on it.

familiar.text: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.

modern.text: Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.

original.text: καὶ ⸀φέρουσιν τὸν πῶλον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ⸀ἐπιβάλλουσιν αὐτῷ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Many spread their garments on the way, and others spread leafy branches cut from the fields.

familiar.text: And many spread their garments in the way: and others cut down branches off the trees, and strawed them in the way.

modern.text: Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.

original.text: ⸂καὶ πολλοὶ⸃ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἔστρωσαν εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, ἄλλοι δὲ στιβάδας ⸂κόψαντες ἐκ τῶν ἀγρῶν⸃.

verses.restored: Those going before and those following cried out, Hosanna! Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord!

familiar.text: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord:

modern.text: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

original.text: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ⸀ἔκραζον· Ὡσαννά· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου·

verses.restored: Blessed is the coming reign of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!

familiar.text: Blessed be the kingdom of our father David, that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.

modern.text: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!” “Hosanna in the highest!”

original.text: Εὐλογημένη ἡ ἐρχομένη ⸀βασιλεία τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Δαυίδ· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.

verses.restored: He entered Jerusalem and the temple. Looking around at everything, since the hour was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.

familiar.text: And Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and into the temple: and when he had looked round about upon all things, and now the eventide was come, he went out unto Bethany with the twelve.

modern.text: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve. Jesus Curses the Fig Tree (Matthew 21:18–22; Mark 11:20–25)

original.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα ⸀ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.

verses.restored: On the next day, when they came out from Bethany, he was hungry.

familiar.text: And on the morrow, when they were come from Bethany, he was hungry:

modern.text: The next day, when they had left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.

original.text: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν.

verses.restored: Seeing from afar a fig tree having leaves, he went to see if perhaps he would find anything on it. Coming to it, he found nothing except leaves, for it was not the season of figs.

familiar.text: And seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came, if haply he might find any thing thereon: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves; for the time of figs was not yet.

modern.text: Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if there was any fruit on it. But when He reached it, He found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs.

original.text: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ⸀ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα ⸂τι εὑρήσει⸃ ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπʼ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα, ⸂ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν⸃ σύκων.

verses.restored: He answered and said to it, May no one eat fruit from you any longer into the age. His disciples were hearing.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto it, No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever. And his disciples heard it.

modern.text: Then He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” And His disciples heard this statement. Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Matthew 21:12–17; Luke 19:45–48; John 2:12–25)

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι ⸂εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ⸃ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι. καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: They came to Jerusalem. Entering the temple, he began to cast out those selling and those buying in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those selling doves.

familiar.text: And they come to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves;

modern.text: When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

original.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ ⸀εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ⸀τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν

verses.restored: He would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.

familiar.text: And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple.

modern.text: And He would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ,

verses.restored: He was teaching and saying to them, Has it not been written: My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations? But you have made it a cave of robbers.

familiar.text: And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.

modern.text: Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’ ? But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”

original.text: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ⸂καὶ ἔλεγεν⸃ ⸀αὐτοῖς· Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν; ὑμεῖς δὲ ⸀πεποιήκατε αὐτὸν σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.

verses.restored: The chief priests and scribes heard and were seeking how they might destroy him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was struck with wonder at his teaching.

familiar.text: And the scribes and chief priests heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because all the people was astonished at his doctrine.

modern.text: When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him. For they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.

original.text: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ⸂ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς⸃, καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν, ⸂πᾶς γὰρ⸃ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: When evening came, they went out of the city.

familiar.text: And when even was come, he went out of the city.

modern.text: And when evening came, Jesus and His disciples went out of the city. The Withered Fig Tree (Matthew 21:18–22; Mark 11:12–14)

original.text: Καὶ ⸀ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο, ⸀ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως.

verses.restored: Passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.

familiar.text: And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.

modern.text: As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.

original.text: Καὶ ⸂παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ⸃ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν.

verses.restored: Peter remembered and said to him, Rabbi, look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered.

familiar.text: And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.

modern.text: Peter remembered it and said, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.”

original.text: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται.

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Have trust of the Divine.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.

modern.text: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετε πίστιν θεοῦ·

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: whoever says to this mountain, Be lifted up and thrown into the sea, and does not doubt/divide in the heart but trusts that what is spoken happens, it will be for that one.

familiar.text: For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith.

modern.text: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.

original.text: ⸀ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ μὴ διακριθῇ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ⸀πιστεύῃ ὅτι ⸂ὃ λαλεῖ γίνεται, ἔσται αὐτῷ⸃.

verses.restored: Because of this I say to you: all things whatever you pray and ask, trust that you received, and it will be for you.

familiar.text: Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.

modern.text: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πάντα ὅσα ⸂προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε⸃, πιστεύετε ὅτι ⸀ἐλάβετε, καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Whenever you stand praying, release if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father in the heavens also may release you your trespasses.

familiar.text: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.

modern.text: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well. ” Jesus’ Authority Challenged (Matthew 21:23–27; Luke 20:1–8)

original.text: καὶ ὅταν ⸀στήκετε προσευχόμενοι, ἀφίετε εἴ τι ἔχετε κατά τινος, ἵνα καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφῇ ὑμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα ⸀ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add: But if you do not release, neither will your Father in the heavens release your trespasses.]

familiar.text: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.

modern.note: The BSB follows modern critical-text practice here and does not print this traditional verse number as a separate verse.

original.note: This traditional verse number is not present as a separate verse in the SBLGNT base text; preserve as a textual-witness issue.

verses.restored: They came again into Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders came to him,

familiar.text: And they come again to Jerusalem: and as he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders,

modern.text: After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.

original.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται πάλιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ περιπατοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι

verses.restored: and said to him, By what authority do you do these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?

familiar.text: And say unto him, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority to do these things?

modern.text: “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You the authority to do them?”

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; ⸀ἢ τίς σοι ⸂ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην⸃ ἵνα ταῦτα ποιῇς;

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, I will ask you one word; answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

modern.text: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐπερωτήσω ⸀ὑμᾶς ἕνα λόγον, καὶ ἀποκρίθητέ μοι, καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·

verses.restored: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from humans? Answer me.

familiar.text: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? answer me.

modern.text: John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”

original.text: τὸ βάπτισμα ⸀τὸ Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων; ἀποκρίθητέ μοι.

verses.restored: They reasoned among themselves, saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say, Why then did you not trust him?

familiar.text: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did ye not believe him?

modern.text: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

original.text: καὶ ⸀διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες· ⸂Τί εἴπωμεν;⸃ ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί ⸀οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;

verses.restored: But shall we say, From humans? They feared the crowd, for all held John to truly be a prophet.

familiar.text: But if we shall say, Of men; they feared the people: for all men counted John, that he was a prophet indeed.

modern.text: But if we say, ‘From men’...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.

original.text: ἀλλὰ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;— ἐφοβοῦντο τὸν ⸀ὄχλον, ἅπαντες γὰρ εἶχον τὸν Ἰωάννην ⸂ὄντως ὅτι⸃ προφήτης ἦν.

verses.restored: Answering Jesus, they said, We do not know. Jesus said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

familiar.text: And they answered and said unto Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus answering saith unto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

modern.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες ⸂τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγουσιν⸃· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν. καὶ ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
